Radial-velocity dataset seed45_diff4.

- 56 observations over a baseline of 282.7 days
- median reported uncertainty: 2.51 m/s
- instruments: instA

Recover the planetary system that produced this signal: the number of
planets and each one's orbital parameters. The data is available to your
tools; you do not need it inlined here.

A submission passes only if it satisfies all four criteria at once: the
model must beat a flat line (delta-BIC), the residual scatter must be
within 1.5x the median reported uncertainty, the orbits must match the
underlying system, and the planet count must be right. A good statistical
fit at the wrong period fails.

Initial hypothesis: 1 planet.

Primary candidate period:
- 188.49 d

Why this period:
- It is by far the dominant peak in the periodogram, with very high power and extremely low approximate FAP (~4.7e-12).
- It is below the 282.7 d observing baseline, so it is at least constrained by the data.
- The obvious relatives are:
  - half-period: 94.24 d
  - double-period: 376.98 d
  - 1-day aliases near 1.00 d
- None of those relatives appears comparably compelling in the returned peak list.
- There is also a weaker peak at 88.36 d, but that is close to the half-period family of the 188.49 d signal and is much less significant, so I would treat it as harmonic/related structure rather than a separate planet at this stage.
- The short-period peaks near 0.6–1.4 d have poor significance and sit in the regime where daily cadence aliases are common; they are not good first-planet hypotheses.

Plan for the engineer:
- Fit a 1-planet Keplerian at P ≈ 188.49 d first.
- After fitting, inspect residuals to decide whether any additional planet remains, with special attention to whether the ~88–94 d structure survives independently or disappears as a harmonic/alias of the long-period signal.
